card.title: You have one minute to prepare.

bubbles.t: Starting next month, you can work from home.

card.start: One day, a woman was talking with her coworkers in the office.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, let's start the test. Here is your card.
You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman who started working from home. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
All right. Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 2. Do you think companies should allow more employees to work from home?

narr.ja: 4コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から2分で説明してください。
model: One day, a woman was talking with her coworkers in the office. Her boss said to them, "Starting next month, you can work from home." The woman looked happy to hear this. A month later, she was working on her computer at home. She was drinking coffee, and her dog was sitting next to her. A few weeks later, there was construction work near her house. It was very noisy, and she couldn't concentrate on her work. The next week, she was working at the office again, and she was talking with her boss.
points: 4コマすべて + コマ間の言葉(A month later など)
吹き出しのセリフ・表情も説明
1分の準備で各コマ1〜2文を決める

q1.q: If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
q1.ja: あなたがこの女性だったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
model: I'd be thinking, "Working from home was comfortable, but it's easier to concentrate at the office. Maybe I should come to the office on some days."

q2.q: Do you think companies should allow more employees to work from home?
q2.ja: 会社はもっと多くの社員に在宅勤務を認めるべきだと思いますか。
model: Yes. Employees can save time because they don't have to commute. As a result, they may have more energy for their work and their families.
points: 意見 + 理由 + 結果(As a result)

card.title: You have one minute to prepare.
card.start: One day, a man was having a health checkup at a hospital.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, let's start the test. Here is your card.
You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who wanted to get more exercise. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
All right. Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 2. Do you think companies should do more to help their employees stay healthy?

narr.ja: 4コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から2分で説明してください。
model: One day, a man was having a health checkup at a hospital. The doctor said to him, "You should get more exercise." The man looked worried. The next week, he joined a gym. He was lifting weights, and a trainer was giving him advice. A few weeks later, he was still working at the office late at night. His boss was giving him more documents, and the man was thinking that he couldn't go to the gym. Some time later, the man was riding a bicycle to work. He was sweating a lot, and one of his coworkers looked surprised.
points: 4コマすべて + コマ間の言葉(A month later など)
吹き出しのセリフ・表情も説明
1分の準備で各コマ1〜2文を決める

q1.q: If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
q1.ja: あなたがこの男性だったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
model: I'd be thinking, "Cycling to work is a good way to get exercise without going to the gym. But I should bring a change of clothes."

q2.q: Do you think companies should do more to help their employees stay healthy?
q2.ja: 会社は社員の健康を保つためにもっと取り組むべきだと思いますか。
model: Yes. Healthy employees can work better and take fewer sick days. For example, companies can give workers time to exercise or offer healthy lunches. As a result, the whole company benefits.
points: 意見 + 理由 + 結果(As a result)

card.title: You have one minute to prepare.

bubbles.t: Let's go to Italy this summer!

card.start: One day, a woman and her husband were planning their vacation.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, let's start the test. Here is your card.
You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman who traveled abroad. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
All right. Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 2. Do you think translation technology will make learning foreign languages unnecessary?

narr.ja: 4コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から2分で説明してください。
model: One day, a woman and her husband were planning their vacation. Her husband said to her, "Let's go to Italy this summer!" When they arrived in Italy, the woman was using a translation app on her smartphone to talk to a taxi driver, and her husband was carrying their suitcases. That evening, they went to a restaurant. The waiter was speaking Italian, but the woman's smartphone had no signal, so she couldn't understand him. After the trip, the woman was taking an online Italian lesson at home.
points: 4コマすべて + コマ間の言葉(A month later など)
吹き出しのセリフ・表情も説明
1分の準備で各コマ1〜2文を決める

q1.q: If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
q1.ja: あなたがこの女性だったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
model: I'd be thinking, "Translation apps are useful, but I can't always depend on them. If I learn some Italian, our next trip will be more enjoyable."

q2.q: Do you think translation technology will make learning foreign languages unnecessary?
q2.ja: 翻訳技術によって外国語を学ぶ必要はなくなると思いますか。
model: No. Translation apps are getting better, but they cannot fully show the speaker's feelings or culture. Also, people can build closer relationships when they speak the same language.
points: 意見 + 理由 + 結果(As a result)

card.title: You have one minute to prepare.

bubbles.t: Happy birthday! Here's your first smartphone.

card.start: One day, a girl was celebrating her birthday with her parents.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, let's start the test. Here is your card.
You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a girl who got her first smartphone. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
All right. Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the girl, what would you be thinking?
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 2. Should parents limit how much time their children spend on smartphones?

narr.ja: 4コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から2分で説明してください。
model: One day, a girl was celebrating her birthday with her parents. Her mother said to her, "Happy birthday! Here's your first smartphone." The girl looked very happy. A month later, she was using her smartphone in bed late at night. It was already one o'clock. The next morning, she was sleeping during class, and her teacher was telling her to wake up. That evening, her parents were talking to her about rules for using her smartphone. They decided that she would not use it after 9 p.m.
points: 4コマすべて + コマ間の言葉(A month later など)
吹き出しのセリフ・表情も説明
1分の準備で各コマ1〜2文を決める

q1.q: If you were the girl, what would you be thinking?
q1.ja: あなたがこの女の子だったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
model: I'd be thinking, "I'm sorry that I used my smartphone so late. My parents are right, so I'll follow the rules from now on."

q2.q: Should parents limit how much time their children spend on smartphones?
q2.ja: 親は子どもがスマートフォンを使う時間を制限すべきですか。
model: Yes. Children often cannot control how much time they spend on games and videos. If parents set some rules, their children can get enough sleep and focus on their studies.
points: 意見 + 理由 + 結果(As a result)

card.title: You have one minute to prepare.

bubbles.t: There are too many cars on our street!

card.start: One day, a man was working late at his office in the city.

steps.t: Thank you. Now, let's start the test. Here is your card.
You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who opened a café in the countryside. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
All right. Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
Now, I'll ask you four questions.
Number 1. Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
Now, please turn over the card and put it down.
Number 2. Do you think social media is a good way for small businesses to find customers?

narr.ja: 4コマのイラストの話を、カードの最初の文から2分で説明してください。
model: One day, a man was working late at his office in the city. He saw a poster about life in the countryside, and he was thinking about opening a café there. Half a year later, he had opened a café in a small town, but there were no customers, and he looked worried. A few weeks later, he was taking pictures of his cakes to post on social media. The next month, many people were waiting in line outside his café. However, their cars were parked on the street, and an elderly woman said to him, "There are too many cars on our street!"
points: 4コマすべて + コマ間の言葉(A month later など)
吹き出しのセリフ・表情も説明
1分の準備で各コマ1〜2文を決める

q1.q: If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
q1.ja: あなたがこの男性だったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
model: I'd be thinking, "I'm glad that so many customers are coming, but I don't want to cause trouble for my neighbors. I should find a parking lot for my customers."

q2.q: Do you think social media is a good way for small businesses to find customers?
q2.ja: SNSは小さな店が客を見つける良い方法だと思いますか。
model: Yes. Social media is free and can reach many people quickly. For example, a small café can become popular when customers share photos of its food. As a result, it can compete with big companies.
points: 意見 + 理由 + 結果(As a result)

ekp1_free.q: Please tell me a little about yourself.
ekp1_free.ja: 少し自己紹介をしてください。
model: I'm a high school student. I'm interested in airplanes, and I want to become an airline pilot in the future.

ekp1_free.q: What do you like to do in your free time?
ekp1_free.ja: 自由な時間に何をするのが好きですか。
model: I like riding my bike. On weekends, I often ride to the airport to watch planes.

ekp1_free.q: How did you come here today?
ekp1_free.ja: 今日はどうやってここに来ましたか。
model: I came here by train. It took about thirty minutes.

ekp1_free.q: What are you interested in these days?
ekp1_free.ja: 最近、何に興味がありますか。
model: Recently, I've been interested in learning Korean. I watch Korean dramas to practice.

ekp1_free.ja: 最近どこかに旅行しましたか。
model: Yes. I went to Hokkaido with my family last summer. The food was great.

ekp1_free.q: What do you want to do after you finish school?
ekp1_free.ja: 学校を卒業したら何をしたいですか。
model: I want to go to a university and study engineering. After that, I want to work abroad.

ekp1_s.q: Should the government do more to support small businesses in rural areas?
ekp1_s.ja: 政府は地方の小さな会社をもっと支援すべきですか。
model: Yes. Small businesses create jobs for local people. If they close, young people will move to big cities, and rural areas will become even smaller.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: These days, many people read the news on their smartphones. Do you think people trust the news less than they did in the past?
ekp1_s.ja: 人々は昔よりニュースを信頼しなくなったと思いますか。
model: Yes. There is a lot of false information on the Internet. It is sometimes hard for people to tell which news is true.
points: 前置きの文(These days, …)を受けて答える

ekp1_s.q: Do you think Japan should accept more tourists from abroad?
ekp1_s.ja: 日本は海外からの観光客をもっと受け入れるべきだと思いますか。
model: Yes. Tourists spend a lot of money, and this helps local economies. However, popular places need rules so that they do not become too crowded.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: Should schools put more emphasis on teaching students about the environment?
ekp1_s.ja: 学校は環境についての教育にもっと力を入れるべきですか。
model: Yes. Climate change will affect young people the most. If students learn about it early, they can change their habits, such as using less plastic.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: Do you think people today have less free time than in the past?
ekp1_s.ja: 今の人は昔より自由な時間が少ないと思いますか。
model: Yes. Many people work long hours, and smartphones make it hard to stop working after they get home. As a result, they don't have enough time to relax.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: Is it a good idea for companies to hire more older workers?
ekp1_s.ja: 会社がもっと高齢の労働者を雇うのは良い考えですか。
model: Yes. Older workers have a lot of experience and skills. They can also teach young workers, so the whole company benefits.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: Should professional athletes be paid such high salaries?
ekp1_s.ja: プロスポーツ選手の高い給料は妥当だと思いますか。
model: I think so. Athletes train very hard, and their careers are short. They also bring a lot of money to their teams through ticket sales and advertising.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: Do you think artificial intelligence will make people's lives better?
ekp1_s.ja: AIは人々の生活をより良くすると思いますか。
model: Yes, in many ways. AI can help doctors find diseases earlier and make work more efficient. However, we need rules to protect personal information.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: Should more people take part in volunteer activities in their local communities?
ekp1_s.ja: 地域のボランティア活動にもっと多くの人が参加すべきですか。
model: Yes. Local communities have many problems, such as caring for elderly people. If more people volunteer, they can solve these problems together and build stronger relationships.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: Do you think Japan should make more efforts to produce its own food?
ekp1_s.ja: 日本は自国での食料生産にもっと力を入れるべきだと思いますか。
model: Yes. Japan imports much of its food, so prices can rise when there are problems in other countries. Supporting local farmers would make the food supply more stable.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: Is it important for people to keep learning after they start working?
ekp1_s.ja: 働き始めてからも学び続けることは大切ですか。
model: Yes. Technology changes quickly, so the skills people learn at school can soon become out of date. By taking courses, workers can keep up with changes and find better jobs.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎

ekp1_s.q: Should cities do more to reduce the number of cars on their roads?
ekp1_s.ja: 都市は道路を走る車を減らすためにもっと取り組むべきですか。
model: Yes. Cars cause traffic jams and air pollution. If cities improve public transportation and build more bike lanes, people will not need to drive as much.
points: 社会全体への影響まで言えると◎
